column1: # sen_sero serovar rules — one row per serovar, in rule order (most specific first).
# serovar    the phenotype name the rule prints
# Rows are grouped: full antigenic-formula rules first, then the generic
# "O group only, H not determined" rows. The document is evaluated with
# decision: most_specific, so a full rule outranks the generic one it implies
# (without that policy both would match and the call would be ambiguous).
# formula    antigenic formula (White-Kauffmann-Le Minor notation) for humans
# requires   ';'-joined marker ids that must ALL be present
# excludes   ';'-joined marker ids that must all be absent (empty = none)
# outranks   ';'-joined gene:competitor,e.g. tyr_A:rfbE_D1 — the named allele must
#            score strictly higher than each competitor (near-identical allele
#            pairs: O:2 vs O:9 are 98.5-99.2% identical, so presence cannot
#            separate them; this is SeqSero2's 'tyr-O-2 vs tyr-O-9' comparison)
# notes      ';'-joined free-text caveats carried onto the call
# The panel deliberately keeps the O antigen coarse where the gene content
# cannot decide it (see README: O:2 vs O:9 needs the rfb cluster stage), so a
# serovar whose O group is only distinguishable by a pseudogene is marked
# provisional here.
